svg.title: ln -s: a symbolic link refers to another path.
svg.desc: An existing ordinary file note.txt contains Tea at four. With no shortcut path present, ln -s note.txt shortcut creates a symbolic link storing the relative path note.txt. The arrow leads from the reference to the real file. cat shortcut reads the target. Editing through the link edits the target; deleting only the link retains the target, but a removed or moved target leaves a dangling link.
svg.text: A symbolic link stores a path to another file, not a copy.
Before: ordinary file note.txt exists here. The name shortcut does not.
Command: create the link (-s means symbolic)
A relative target path starts in the directory containing the link (here, this directory).
Output: Tea at four. Editing through the link changes the target.
Delete only the link: target stays. Move/remove target: link dangles (points nowhere).
